issues.description: The template Lecture class defines addGuestStudents with signature addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) whereas the problem statement and the solution expect addGuestStudents(int). This signature mismatch will confuse students and cause their implementations/tests to fail because the template method includes an extra boolean parameter that is not part of the specification or reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template method signature to match the specification and solution: change public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). If input validation is desired, implement it internally (e.g., validate the int parameter inside the method) or provide an overloaded helper method without changing the specified signature.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a method addGuestStudents(int) but the template declares addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput). The solution implements addGuestStudents(int). This signature mismatch (extra boolean parameter only in the template) breaks the direct mapping from the exercise requirements to the starter code and the reference solution, and will confuse students and tests that expect a single-parameter method.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem statement and solution by changing the template method signature to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } . Alternatively, provide an overloaded addGuestStudents(int) that delegates to the two-parameter version, but ensure the single-parameter signature required by the task and tests is present.
